questions.q:
Sodium oxide reacts with water to produce sodium hydroxide. $20 . 0g$ of sodium oxide is dissolved in $500mL$ of water. Neglecting the change in volume, the concentration of the resulting $NaOH$ solution is _________~$\times {10}^{- 1}M .$~(Nearest integer)
[Atomic mass : $Na = 23 . 0, O = 16 . 0, H = 1 . 0$]
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.solution:
${Na}_{2}O + {H}_{2}O \to 2NaOH$
According to reaction $\dfrac{20}{62}$ mole of ${Na}_{2}O$ gives $\dfrac{40}{62}$ mole of $NaOH$
so molarity of $NaOH$ solution is $= \dfrac{nNaOH}{Vml} \times 1000 = \dfrac{40}{62} \times \dfrac{1000}{500} = \dfrac{80}{62} = 1 . 29M \approx 1 . 3M$

questions.q: The Total pressure observed by mixing two liquid $A\text{and}B$ is $350mmHg$ when their mole fractions are~$0 . 7\text{and}0 . 3$ respectively.~The Total pressure becomes$410mmHg$ if the mole fractions are changed to$0 . 2\text{and}0 . 8$ respectively for $A\text{and}B$. The vapour pressure of pure $A$ is ______ $mmHg$. (Nearest integer) Consider the liquids and solutions behave ideally
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.solution:
Let Vapour pressure& of pure $A$~be~${P}_A^{o}$

Let Vapour pressure~of pure $B$~be~${P}_B^{o}$

Using Raoult's law and Dalton's law:

$When{X}_{A} = 0 . 7 \text{ and } {X}_{B} = 0 . 3{P}_{s} = 350 ⇒ {P}_A^{o} \times 0 . 7 + {P}_B^{o} \times 0 . 3 = 350 . . . . ( i ) When{X}_{A} = 0 . 2 \text{ and } {X}_{B} = 0 . 8{P}_{s} = 410 ⇒ {P}_A^{o} \times 0 . 7 + {P}_B^{o} \times 0 . 3 = 350 . . . . ( ii ) Solving ( i ) and ( ii ) {P}_A^{o} = 314mmHg{P}_B^{o} = 434mmHg$

questions.q: When a certain amount of solid $A$ is dissolved in $100g$ of water at $25 ° C$ to make a dilute solution, the vapour pressure of the solution is reduced to one-half of that of pure water. The vapour pressure of pure water is $23 . 76mmHg$. The number of moles of solute $A$ added is
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.solution:
We know that relative lowering in vapour pressure is given as

$\dfrac{P^{0} - {P}_{S}}{Po} = \dfrac{solute n}{{n}_{Solute} + solvent n}$

$\dfrac{P^{0} - {P}_{S}}{PS} = \dfrac{solute n}{solvent n}$

$\dfrac{P^{0} - \dfrac{P0}{2}}{\dfrac{P0}{2}} = \dfrac{solute n}{solvent n}$

$solute n = solvent n = \dfrac{100}{18} = 5 . 55mol$

questions.q:
${CO}_{2}$ gas is bubbled through water during a soft drink manufacturing process at $298K$. If ${CO}_{2}$ exerts a partial pressure of $0 . 835bar$ then $xmmol$~of ${CO}_{2}$ would dissolve in $0 . 9L$ of water. The value of $x$ is _______. (Nearest integer)

(Henry's law constant for ${CO}_{2}$ at $298K$ is $1 . 67 \times {10}^{3}bar$)
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.solution:
From Henry's law

${P}_{gas} = {K}_{H \cdot}{X}_{gas}$

$0 . 835 = 1 . 67 \times {10}^{3} \times \dfrac{n\left({CO}_{2}\right)}{0 . 9 \times 100018}$

$n\left({CO}_{2}\right) = 0 . 025$

Millimoles of ${CO}_{2} = 0 . 025 \times 1000 = 25$

questions.q: The osmotic pressure of a dilute solution is $7 \times {10}^{5}Pa$ at $273K$. Osmotic pressure of the same solution at $283K$ is _______ \times {10}^{4}{Nm}^{- 2}.(Nearest integer)
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.solution:
Osmotic pressure can be calculated as,

$\pi = CRT$

π is the osmotic pressure

C is the molar concentration of the solute in the solution

R is the universal gas constant

Here given,

${T}_{1} = 273K{T}_{2} = 283K$

${π}_{1} = {CRT}_{1}\text{By putting the values in this equation, we get,}7 \times {10}^{5} = C \times R \times 273CR = \dfrac{7 \times {10}^{5}}{273}{π}_{2} = {CRT}_{2} = \dfrac{7 \times {10}^{5}}{273} \times 283 = 72 . 56 \times {10}^{4}{Nm}^{- 2}$

questions.q:
Ferrous sulphate heptahydrate is used to fortify foods with iron. The amount (in grams) of the salt required to achieve $10$ ppm of iron in $100$ kg of wheat is ____________.
Atomic weight: $Fe = 55.85; S = 32.00; O = 16.00$
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.solution:
Formula of& $p$ pm~is as follow-

$ppm = \dfrac{weightofsolute}{weightofsolution} \times {10}^{6}$

$10 = \dfrac{MassofFe ( ing )}{100 \times 1000} \times {10}^{6}$
Or mass fe $= 1g$
$FeS{O}_{4} . 7{H}_{2}O \left(M = 278\right)$
56g in 1 mole
$1g - $\dfrac{1}{56}$mole$
\dfrac{1}{56} \times$278g = 4.96g

PPM is a concentration term and its full form is "parts per million" and it also can be expressed as milligrams per liter (mg/L). This measurement is the mass of a chemical or contaminate per unit volume of water.&

$

questions.q:
The vapour pressure of $30 % \left(w / v\right)$,~aqueous solution of glucose is~________ $mmHg$ at ${25}^{∘}C$.

[Given: The density of $30 % \left(w / v\right)$, aqueous solution of glucose is $1 . 2g{cm}^{– 3}$ and vapour pressure of pure water is $24mmHg$.]

(Molar mass of glucose is $180g{mol}^{– 1}$)
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.solution:
To calculate the vapour pressure of the $30 %$ (w/v) aqueous solution of glucose, we can use Raoult's law, which states that the vapour pressure of a component in an ideal solution is directly proportional to its mole fraction in the solution.

Weight of solution $= 100 \times 1 . 2 = 120gm$

Weight of water $= 120 - 30 = 90gm$

Now using formula

$\dfrac{{P}_{0} - P}{P} = \dfrac{molesof glucose}{molesof water}$

$\dfrac{24 - P}{P} = \dfrac{30180}{9018} = \dfrac{3}{90}$

$24 \times 90 - P \times 90 = 3P$

$⇒ P = 23 . 22$

questions.q:
A solution containing (10 $\mathrm{~g}$) of an electrolyte ($\mathrm{AB}}_{2}) in (100 \mathrm{~g}) of water boils at (100.52^{{}^{{}^{\circ}}} $\mathrm{C}$). The degree of ionization of the electrolyte ((\alpha)) is _______ (\times10^{-1}). (nearest integer)
[Given : Molar mass of (\mathrm{AB}}_{2}=200 $\mathrm{~g} \mathrm{~mol}^{-1}, \mathrm{~K}_{\mathrm{b}}$) (molal boiling point elevation const. of water) (=0.52 $\mathrm{~K} \mathrm{~kg} \mathrm{~mol}^{-1}$), boiling point of water (=100^{{}^{{}^{\circ}}} $\mathrm{C}$; $\mathrm{AB}}_{2}) ionises as ( \left.\mathrm{AB}}_{2} \rightarrow \mathrmA^{2+}+2 \mathrm{~B}^{-}\right])
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.solution:
$\begin{aligned} & \mathrm{AB}_2 \rightarrow \mathrmA^{+2}+2 \mathrm{~B}^{\ominus} \\ & \mathrm{i}=1+(3-1) \alpha \\ & \mathrm{i}=1+2 \alpha \\ & \Delta \mathrm{T}_{\mathrm{b}}=\mathrm{k}_{\mathrm{b}} \mathrm{im} \\ & 0.52=0.52(1+2 \alpha) \frac{\frac{10}{200}}{\frac{100}{1000}} \\ & 1=(1+2 \alpha) \frac{10}{20} \\ & 2=1+2 \alpha \\ & \alpha=0.5\end{aligned}$
Ans. $\alpha=5 \times 10^{-1}$

questions.q: At $300K$, the vapour pressure of a solution containing $1$ mole of $n$ -hexane and $3$ moles of $n$ -heptane is $550$ mm of $Hg$. At the same temperature, if one more mole of $n$ -heptane is added to this solution, the vapour pressure of the solution increases by $10$ mm of $Hg$. What is the vapour pressure in $mmHg$ of $n$ - heptane in its pure state______?
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.solution:
${P}_{total} = P^{∘}hexane . {X}_{hexane} + P^{∘}heptane . {X}_{heptane}$

$550 = \left[P^{∘}hexane\right] \times \dfrac{1}{4} + \left[P^{∘}heptane\right] \times \dfrac{3}{4}$~ ~ ~..$( i )$

After mixing~$1$~mole n-heptane

$560 = \left[P^{∘}hexane\right] \times \dfrac{1}{5} + \left[P^{∘}heptane\right] \times \dfrac{4}{5}$~ ~ ~.....$( ii )$

On solving eq. (i) and (ii)

$P^{∘}heptane = 600mm$~of~$Hg$

questions.q: Molality of an aqueous solution of urea is (4.44 $\mathrm{~m}$). Mole fraction of urea in solution is (x $\times$10^{-3}). Value of $x$ is (\qquad) - (Integer answer)
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.solution:
Molality of urea is $4.44 \mathrm{~m}$, that means 4.44 moles of urea present in $1000 \mathrm{gm}$ of water.
$\therefore \mathrm{X}_{\text {ura }}=\frac{4.44}{4.44+\frac{1000}{18}}=0.0740$
OR
$\begin{aligned} & 74 \times 10^{-3} \\ & X=74\end{aligned}$

questions.q: The elevation in boiling point for& $1$ molal solution of non-volatile solute $A$ is $3K$. The depression in freezing point for~$2$~molal solution of $A$ in the same solvent is $6K$. The ratio of ${K}_{b}$ and ${K}_{f}$ i.e., ${K}_{b} / {K}_{f}$ is $1: X$. The value of $X$ is
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.solution:
We know that

${ΔT}_{b} = {iK}_{b}{m}_{1}{ΔT}_{f} = {iK}_{f}{m}_{2}$

And for non-volatile solute~$i = 1$.

$\dfrac{\Delta Tb}{\Delta Tf} = \dfrac{{K}_{b} \times 1}{{K}_{f} \times 2} ⇒ \dfrac{3}{6} = \dfrac{1}{2} = \dfrac{Kb}{Kf} \times \dfrac{1}{2}$

$\dfrac{Kb}{Kf} = \dfrac{1}{1} ⇒ X = 1$

questions.q:
A $300mL$ bottle of soft drink has $0 . 2{MCO}_{2}$~dissolved in it. Assuming ${CO}_{2}$~behaves as an ideal gas, the volume of the dissolved ${CO}_{2}$~at STP is _____~$mL$. (Nearest integer)

Given: At STP, molar volume of an ideal gas is~$22 . 7L{mol}^{- 1}$
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.solution:
Moles dissolved in soft drinks of& ${CO}_{2} = molarity \times volume = 0 . 2M \times \left(300 \times {10}^{- 3}\right)L$

$= 0 . 06\text{Mole}$

Volume of $0 . 06moleof{CO}_{2}$~at S.T.P

$= 0 . 06 \times 22 . 7$

$= 1 . 362L$

questions.q: The vapour pressures of $A$ and $B$ at $25 ° C$ are $90mmHg$ and $15mmHg$~respectively. If $A$ and $B$ are mixed such that the mole fraction of $A$ in the mixture is $0 . 6,$ then the mole fraction of $B$ in the vapour phase is $x \times {10}^{- 1} .$~The value of $x$ is (Nearest integer)
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.solution:
Given ${P}_{A} ° = 90mmHg,$~at $25 ° C$

${P}_{B} = ∘ 15mmHg$

and~\left
{X}_{A} = 0 . 6
{X}_{B} = 0 . 4
\right\}{P}_{T} = {X}_{A}{P}_A^{o} + {X}_{B}{P}_B^{o}$

$= ( 0 . 6 \times 90 ) + ( 0 . 4 \times 15 )$

$= 54 + 6 = 60mm$

Now mol fraction of $B$ in the vapour phase

i.e.~${Y}_{B} = \dfrac{PB}{PT} = \dfrac{{X}_{B}{P}_B^{o}}{60} = 0 . 1 = 1 \times {10}^{- 1}$

therefore:~$x = 1$

$

questions.q:
The elevation of boiling point of& $0 . 10m$ aqueous~${CrCl}_{3} . {xNH}_{3}$ solution is two times that of~$0 . 05m$ aqueous ${CaCl}_{2}$ solution. The value of $x$~is $\ldots \ldots \ldots \ldots . .$
[Assume $100 %$ ionisation of the complex and ${CaCl}_{2},$ coordination number of $Cr$ as $6,$ and that all ${NH}_{3}$ molecules are present inside the coordination sphere]
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.solution:
$0 . 05m$ aqueous ${CaCl}_{2}= 0 . 15$molal solution of non electrolyte

Since the elevation in boiling point is double so the molality of given solution of complex $= 0 . 3m$

Hence the complex must be producing three ions in the solution, so its formula $= \left[Cr\left({NH}_{3}\right)5Cl\right]{Cl}_{2}$

SO $X = 5$

questions.q: The mass of sodium acetate  \left({CH}_{3}COONa\right)$ required to prepare $250mL$ of $0 . 35M$ aqueous solution is _____ g.  \left(\right$ Molar mass of ${CH}_{3}COONa$ is $82 . 02g{mol}^{- 1}$) Round off to the nearest integer.
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.solution:
Given, Molarity= $0 . 35M$

Moles = Molarity $\times$ Volume in litres

$= 0 . 35 \times 0 . 25$

No. of moles = Mass/ Molar mass

Mass = moles $\times$molar mass

$= 0 . 35 \times 0 . 25 \times 82 . 02 = 7 . 18g$

Ans. $7$

questions.q: At $363K$, the vapour pressure of $A$ is $21$ kPa and that of $B$ is $18$ kPa. One mole of $A$ and $2$~moles of $B$ are mixed. Assuming that this solution is ideal, the vapour pressure of the mixture is___________~$kPa$. $($Round of to the Nearest Integer$)$.
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.solution:
Given ${P}_A^{0} = 21kPa ⇒ {P}_B^{0} = 18kPa$

→ An Ideal solution is prepared by mixing $1$~mole $A and $2$ mole $B$.

$\to {X}_{A} = \dfrac{1}{3}$ and ${X}_{B} = \dfrac{2}{3}$

→ According to Raoult's law

${P}_{T} = {X}_{A}{P}_A^{0} + {X}_{B}{P}_B^{0}$

$⇒ {P}_{T} = \left(\dfrac{1}{3} \times21\right) + \left(\dfrac{2}{3} \times18)$

$⇒ {P}_{T} = 7 + 12 = 19kPa$

$

questions.q:
$1 . 2mL$ of acetic acid is dissolved in water to make~$2 . 0L$ of solution. The depression in freezing point observed for this strength of acid is $0 . 0198 ° C$. The percentage of dissociation of the acid is (Nearest integer) [Given : Density of acetic acid is $1 . 02g{mL}^{- 1}$~Molar mass of acetic acid is~$60g{mol}^{- 1}$
${K}_{f}\left({H}_{2}O\right) = 1 . 85Kkg{mol}^{- 1}$]
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.solution:
$M = d \times V = 1 . 02 \times 1 . 2 = 1 . 224gm$

Moles of acetic acid $= 0 . 0204$~moles in~$2L$

So molality~$= 0 . 0102mol / kg$

Now~${ΔT}_{f} = i \times {K}_{f} \times m$

$i = 1 + \alpha$ for acetic acid

$0 . 0198 = \left(1 + \alpha\right) \times 1 . 85 \times 0 . 0102$

$\alpha = 0 . 04928$

$≅ 5 %$

questions.q:
Some amount of dichloromethane \left({CH}_{2}{Cl}_{2}\right)$ is added to $671 . 141mL$ of chloroform \left({CHCl}_{3}\right)$ to prepare $2 . 6 \times {10}^{- 3}M$ solution of ${CH}_{2}{Cl}_{2} \left(DCM\right)$. The concentration of $DCM$~is _____ ppm (by mass).

Given: Atomic mass : $C = 12; H: 1; Cl = 35 . 5$~density of ${CHCl}_{3} = 1 . 49g{cm}^{- 3}

$
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.solution:
$Molarity = \dfrac{mole}{VolumeinL} = \dfrac{mass / Molarmass}{VolumeinL}$

$2 . 6 \times {10}^{- 3} = \dfrac{x / 85}{0 . 67141}$

$x = 0 . 148g$

The number of ppm~$= \dfrac{massofsolute}{massofsolution} \times {10}^{6}$

Mass of solution = density of solution$\times$Volume of solution

~$DCM$~in ppm $= \dfrac{0 . 148}{1 . 49 \times 671 . 141} \times {10}^{6}$

$= 148ppm$.

questions.q:
$80$~mole percent of ${MgCl}_{2}$ is dissociated in aqueous solution. The vapour pressure of $1 . 0$ molal aqueous solution of ${MgCl}_{2}$~at ${38}^{o}C$~is _____ $mmHg$. (Nearest integer)

Given: Vapour pressure of water at ${38}^{o}C$~is $50mmHg$
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.solution:
One molal solution means one of solute present in one kg of solvent.

${MgCl}_{2}\overset{}{⇌}{Mg}^{2 +} + 2{Cl}^{-}1001 - 0 . 80 . 81 . 6$

Hence, overall moles~after dissociation~$= 2 . 6$

The relative lowering of vapour pressure

$\dfrac{p^{o} - {p}_{s}}{po} = \dfrac{molesofsolute}{molesofsolute + molesofsolvent}$

$\dfrac{p ° - {p}_{s}}{p °} = \dfrac{2 . 6}{\dfrac{1000}{18} + 2 . 6}$

For dilute solution

$\dfrac{p ° - {p}_{s}}{p °} = \dfrac{2 . 6}{\dfrac{1000}{18}}$

$p = 47 . 66 ≃ 48mmHg$

questions.q:
A $0 . 5$~percent solution of potassium chloride was found to freeze at $- 0 . 24 ° C$. The percentage dissociation of potassium chloride is (Nearest integer)
(Molal depression constant for water is $1 . 80Kkg{mol}^{- 1}$ and molar mass of $KCl$ is $74 . 6g{mol}^{- 1}$)
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.solution:
$KCl \to K^{+} + {Cl}^{-}$

$1 - -$

$1 - \alpha\alpha\alpha$

$i = 1 - \alpha + 2\alpha = 1 + \alpha$

$∆ {T}_{f} = i{K}_{f} \cdot m$

$0 . 24 = \left(1 + \alpha\right)1 . 80 \times \dfrac{0 . 5}{74 . 6} \times \dfrac{1000}{99 . 5}$

$\alpha = 0 . 98\alpha % = 98 %$
